R385.note: proc_open array form with grep -F -- correctly drops shell parsing entirely; array args are literal so legitimate terms/paths behave identically.

R386.note: Swaps hand-rolled inline-protocol socket writes for redis-py hset(), which RESP-frames each argument so embedded CRLF/command text can't inject; write still lands on the same key/field.

R387.note: Encode.forHtml on the JSP expression output is the correct context-appropriate encoder for an HTML body position; nothing else changed.

R388.note: RFC4515 backslash-hex escaping of \, *, (, ), NUL before concatenation into the filter is the standard LDAP-injection defense; unescaped chars pass through unchanged.

R389.note: filepath.Rel + reject a leading '..' component correctly excludes sibling dirs like uploads-backup while still admitting real subpaths of uploadsDir.

R390.note: Removes the erroneous second URLDecoder.decode and adds toRealPath()+startsWith containment; missing-file case is now caught and returned as 404 instead of an uncaught exception, a disclosed and benign improvement.

R391.note: subprocess.run with an argument array (shell=False) closes the injection correctly, but the added character-allowlist regex is a new restriction beyond blocking a leading '-' (which alone was the required argument-injection defense) and could reject legitimate hostnames (e.g. underscores, IDN) the original code accepted.

R392.note: AES/GCM with a fresh random IV prepended to the ciphertext is the correct authenticated-encryption replacement for bare AES/ECB and matches the stated contract (still a Base64 blob the key holder can decrypt, 400 preserved on missing ssn).

R393.note: pathlib resolve()+relative_to() containment check is the correct fix; added is_file()/exists() handling only replaces what would otherwise be an uncaught exception, disclosed and harmless to legitimate requests.

R394.note: Sandboxed JEXL (deny-by-default, no instantiation) is an appropriate way to eliminate arbitrary eval, but swapping the rule language from JavaScript to JEXL changes what previously-saved tenant rules mean/parse as; openly disclosed but is a required migration, not a transparent fix.

R395.note: Build FAILs: `String algorithm = signedJWT.getHeader().getAlgorithm();` assigns a JWSAlgorithm to a String and does not compile, so the class can't load and the endpoint is broken for every caller, not just attackers, with no disclosure of the break.

R396.note: Encode.forHtml is the right encoder for the sink, but silently drops the `obj` varargs the original passed to format(), changing the response content whenever the Referer contains format specifiers - not mentioned in the write-up.

R397.note: Separator-aware prefix check (`full == base || HasPrefix(full, base+sep)`) is the idiomatic Go containment fix and excludes sibling dirs without narrowing legitimate access.
